events.label: Census 2024 U.S. domestic migration and birthplace data

slots.name: county migration share
slots.sentence: Six percent of the population lives in U.S. counties they didn’t live in a year prior.

slots.name: recent migrant share
slots.sentence: The places with the highest percent of recent migrants (up to of 19 percent of their population) are college towns like Ithaca, N.Y., home to Cornell University; Corvallis, Ore., where you’ll find Oregon State University; and military towns like Jacksonville, N.C., the site of the massive Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune; and Hinesville, Ga., home to Fort Stewart, a large army base.

slots.name: Savannah newcomer share
slots.sentence: Savannah, Ga., stands out as one of the few places with a population consisting of more than 10 percent of newcomers that is not primarily a military or college town.

slots.name: Charleston newcomer share
slots.sentence: Two hours away in Charleston, S.C., newcomers make up 9 percent of the population, the data shows.

slots.name: out-of-state resident share
slots.sentence: A wider view shows that 41 percent of U.S. residents live in states they weren’t born in.

slots.name: Florida metro count
slots.sentence: In the list of the top 10 metros with the highest share of people born out-of-state, retirement and resort towns dominated, with Florida locales occupying five of the 10 spots.
